footer.tagline: A sailing lugger from 1915, ready for a new adventure.

home.heroIntro: Discover the world of sailing aboard this historic lugger. Built in 1915 as a fishing vessel, converted to a passenger ship in 1980 — and now ready for a new chapter.
home.shipBody: A historic sailing lugger with character. Built in 1915 as a fishing vessel, converted to a passenger ship in 1980 — and ready for new adventures.

spec.typeVal: Sailing lugger — gaff rig, two masts

home.aboutBody: In April 2025 we bought the sailing ship Marie Galante together. Since 2015 she has been moored in the Veerhaven in Rotterdam — and together we want to bring her back to the Baltic Sea to offer guests an active sailing holiday.
home.aboutBody2: Follow the adventure, come and spend a night on board, or dive into the remarkable history of this ship.
home.trackerTitle: Follow the ship live on the map
home.trackerBody: Curious where the Marie Galante is sailing or anchored right now? Watch her live position via MarineTraffic — realtime, anywhere.
home.instaTitle: From the shipyard to the Baltic — a new story every week.

boek.intro: Wind in the sails, the horizon ahead — Marie Galante is waiting for you. Choose a sailing trip on the Baltic, a day trip from a seaside town, an overnight stay on board in winter in Rotterdam, or celebrate aboard a historic ship.

oostzee.title: Sailing the Baltic
oostzee.body: Step aboard for a sailing trip on the Baltic, discover hidden port towns and sail along on a historic ship with a story.

dag.title: Day trips
dag.body: Sail with us for a day from one of the seaside towns on the Baltic. Hoist the sails, feel the wind and experience how a historic lugger glides through the water — no experience needed.

bnb.title: Stay in the Veerhaven
bnb.body: During the winter months Marie Galante is moored at the quay in Rotterdam. Sleep in one of the historic cabins on deck, wake up with a view of the Erasmusbrug and enjoy coffee in the saloon — a unique stay in the heart of the city.

feest.title: A party on board
feest.body: Birthday, company outing or wedding — Marie Galante offers a unique location at the quay. Bar, deck and saloon are available for groups of up to 36 people.

boek.ctaBody: We're happy to think along — an evening at the quay, a week on the Baltic or anything in between.

dag.intro: Step aboard the Marie Galante for a trip from one of the seaside towns on the Baltic. Hoist the sails, feel the wind and experience how a historic lugger glides through the water.
dag.praktischBody: A day on the water with Lex and Lotte at the helm. No experience needed — helping out is welcome, watching is fine too. Bring warm clothing and sunscreen; the sea breeze can be cool and the sun bright. Drinks are available on board and paid in cash.

spec.inbegrepenVal: Coffee, tea and lunch on board

dag.ticketsBody: Our tickets are sold through Weeztix. The ticket shop will appear below as soon as the first dates are announced.
dag.shopBody: The Weeztix ticket shop will appear here. Send us the embed code as soon as your shop is ready and we'll place it here.
dag.charterBody: We also offer day trips where you can charter the entire ship — for groups of up to 36 people, perfect for a company outing or family day. A trip from 10:00 to 17:00, including a welcome drink, coffee and tea. Additional drinks can be paid for on board, or pick a drinks package.

charterTable.lunchIncl: Beer, soft drinks & wine + a warm ship's meal

meevaren.intro: Step aboard Marie Galante for a week of sailing with a group of friends. Hoist the sails together, find an anchorage together, holiday together. Wind in your hair, the Danish islands sliding by, a new view every day.
meevaren.indelingBody: Marie Galante is no luxury yacht — she's a working ship with character. Wooden panelling, brass lamps and bunks where you can hear the water against the hull.

indeling.salonVal: Spacious galley, library, bar and dining area for the whole crew
indeling.sanitairVal: Two toilets and two hot showers
indeling.tuigVal: Two masts, gaff rig — built in 2026

meevaren.gebiedBody: We follow the wind along the German coast and set course for the Danish islands. Every trip is different — the wind decides where we moor.
meevaren.gebiedNote: Indicative sailing area — the exact route follows wind and weather
meevaren.sfeerBody: Early mornings with coffee on deck, long days under sail and evenings in unfamiliar harbours where the beer is local and the sun sets late.
meevaren.faqBody: The most common questions in a row. Don't see yours? Drop us an email.

faq.a1: No. Everyone is welcome, from complete beginner to seasoned sailor. The permanent crew sails the ship — you can join in as much as you like, from hoisting sails to taking the helm.
faq.a2: Prices depend on the duration and the type of trip. Get in touch for current rates, no strings attached.
faq.q3: What does a day on board look like?
faq.a3: Early morning coffee on deck, then we sail to the next harbour or anchorage. We lunch on board along the way and have dinner together in the evening — in port or at anchor.
faq.a4: Warm layered clothing, a rain jacket, sailing or waterproof trousers, sunglasses, a sleeping bag or bedding (we'll let you know in advance) and a good mood — and don't forget your toothbrush. Hard to borrow that one at home.
faq.a5: A maximum of 18 guests in 7 cabins, plus the permanent crew. Cabins are for 2 or 3 people.
faq.a6: The Baltic is a relatively sheltered sea. We sail close to the coast and between the islands, so heavy waves are rare. In doubt? Bring seasickness pills for the first day.

meevaren.ctaBody: In 2026 we hoist the sails for the first time in 10 years. Joining us? Send us an email and we'll look at availability together.

history.intro: A rough outline of the ship's life is known, but many stories are still missing. Have something to add? Been on a memorable voyage?
